profile.entities: Techno Electric & Engineering Company Limited; Kalpataru JV (divested); SEBs; CPSUs; DISCOMs
profile.subseg: FGD Systems; Transmission Infrastructure; AMI Smart Meters; Wind Power; Data Centers; Energy Storage
profile.themes: Green Corridors; Data Centers; Energy Storage; Power Sector Reforms; Carbon-Neutral Infrastructure

bull_bear.body: Debt-free with INR 1,200cr net cash; prioritizing data center and energy storage CapEx; potential dividends and share buyback post market stability; monetization of land bank and other assets; strategic JVs to fund data center projects
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body: Delay in FGD order conversion beyond March 2022; execution delays in data center due to design complexity; regulatory delays in REC trading or tariff approvals; geopolitical supply chain disruptions for electromechanical components; slower-than-expected DISCOM reforms; competition in data center market from hyperscalers
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body: Highly optimistic and transformational; management emphasizes shift from 'EPC company' to 'technology solution provider'; confident in long-term power sector reforms; proactive on data centers and energy storage; transparent on one-offs and margin pressures; focused on sustainability and ESG alignment
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body: REC certificate trading is a recurring revenue stream (INR 25cr Q3, INR 20cr expected by March); data center CapEx is largely in-house EPC (60%), enabling margin retention; Chennai location chosen for undersea cable access and existing renewable assets, not just market demand; wind segment's seasonal loss is structural, not operational failure; INR 1,200cr cash is equivalent to INR 100/share, creating significant hidden value
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

business.body: FGD: INR 1,600cr L1 orders (80GW pipeline over 4 years); Transmission: 765kV project (INR 250cr), TBCB participation (INR 400-500cr potential); AMI: J&K project (50k meters installed, 6L more tendered); Wind: INR 7cr Q3 revenue (ex-REC), 218M units generated (up 5% YoY); Data Centers: Chennai project (30MW, INR 1,200cr CapEx, Phase 1 commissioning by June 2023); Energy Storage: Integrated with data centers and transmission assets

latest_quarter.body: EPC segment margin: 15-16% sustainable; wind segment: 85% margin on REC revenue; data center: 70-75% EBITDA margin at peak; cost pressures from commodity prices and freight partially offset by PV clauses in contracts; O&M cost for wind: INR 14-15cr/quarter
latest_quarter.title: Margins & cost dynamics

outlook.body: EPC revenue to exceed INR 3,000cr in FY22; EBITDA margin to sustain at ~15%; FY23 EPC revenue target of INR 1,500cr+ (ex-data center); data center revenue to contribute INR 400cr+ at peak; EPS to reach INR 50 in 3-4 years
outlook.title: Guidance

outlook.body: INR 1,600cr unexecuted backlog + INR 1,600cr L1 FGD orders (pending execution) + INR 250cr 765kV transmission order (expected by March) = total visibility of INR 3,500cr+
outlook.title: Order book & pipeline

outlook.body: Expansion into 2-3 data centers (Chennai, Kolkata, Mumbai) totaling 200-250MW by 2029; energy storage solutions as complementary to transmission; participation in DISCOM-led distribution reforms; REC certificate trading monetization; potential JV partnerships for data center CapEx
outlook.title: Growth verticals / optionality

deepdive.thesis: Techno Electric is transforming from a traditional EPC player into a technology-driven energy solutions provider, leveraging its strong balance sheet and order book to capture growth in FGD, transmission, data centers, and energy storage amid India's power sector reforms and net-zero ambitions. The company's debt-free position and high cash reserves enable strategic bets on high-margin, long-term infrastructure opportunities.
